summary: Diagnose fit, assumptions, influence, uncertainty, and specification sensitivity before making descriptive, predictive, or causal claims.
triggers: A statistical model needs diagnostics before coefficients or predictions are interpreted.
A conclusion may change under plausible specifications or influential observations.
An evidence report needs an explicit estimand, uncertainty ledger, and claim boundary.
antiTriggers: Claim causality without an identification design.
Issue medical, financial, or legal advice from a model alone.
Hide missingness, leakage, influence, or unstable specifications.

provenance.note: Method source read in full and independently rewritten for portable product use; the historical file remains unchanged.
Estimand, diagnostic, sensitivity, uncertainty, and claim-boundary semantics informed the rewrite; no source prose was copied.
Ownership and evidence boundaries were consulted; no model or domain conclusion is asserted.
